description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved classic in Turkish cuisine, a comforting and hearty red lentil soup known for its creamy texture and rich, savory flavor. This traditional soup is incredibly nutritious and easy to prepare, making it a perfect meal for any day. With a vibrant color and aromatic spices, it promises a warm and satisfying experience that captures the essence of Turkish home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain. Finely chop the onion, carrot, and potato (if using). Mince the garlic.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the chopped carrot and potato (if using) and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Add Garlic, Tomato Paste and Flour
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly to deepen its flavor. If using, sprinkle in the flour and cook for another minute, stirring to combine.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot. Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth (or water). Season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Once the lentils and vegetables are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water to reach your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint Butter
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber). Sizzle for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. This aromatic butter will be drizzled over the soup.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the fragrant mint and pepper butter over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing, as the lemon brightens the flavors beautifully. Enjoy with a slice of crusty Turkish bread.

tips: For an extra smooth soup, pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any tiny bits of lentil skins or vegetables.
The secret to the authentic Mercimek Corbasi flavor lies in the 'nane ve pul biberli tereyagi' (mint and red pepper butter). Do not skip this step!

Mercimek Corbasi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if it has thickened.
article:
Turkish cuisine is a vibrant tapestry of flavors, deeply rooted in history and hospitality. From sizzling kebabs to delectable baklava, each dish tells a story. Among the many culinary treasures, one stands out for its comforting warmth, nourishing simplicity, and universal appeal: Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This humble yet incredibly flavorful soup is a staple in Turkish homes and restaurants alike, served at almost every meal, from breakfast to dinner.

Imagine a bowl of creamy, ruby-hued goodness, fragrant with mint and spices, ready to warm your soul. That's the essence of Mercimek Corbasi. It's more than just a soup; it's a hug in a bowl, a taste of Turkish tradition that transcends borders. Whether you're seeking a hearty starter, a light lunch, or a soothing remedy on a chilly day, this classic lentil soup offers a delightful experience. Its popularity isn't just due to its exquisite taste; it's also incredibly nutritious, easy to make, and remarkably versatile, making it a favorite for home cooks around the world.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi (pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-SUH) is a traditional Turkish soup made primarily from red lentils. It's renowned for its smooth, creamy texture and a rich, savory flavor profile, often brightened by a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Unlike some lentil soups that might be chunky, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed until silky, offering a velvety mouthfeel that is incredibly satisfying.

At its heart, this soup embodies the philosophy of using simple, wholesome ingredients to create something extraordinary. The base consists of red lentils, which cook down quickly and provide a natural creaminess. These are typically sautéed with onions and garlic, then simmered with tomato paste and water or broth. The magic often happens at the end, with the addition of a special butter-based topping (nane yağı) infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber), which adds a crucial layer of aromatic depth and a gentle kick. Mercimek Corbasi isn't just food; it's a cultural cornerstone, a symbol of comfort and sustenance that has graced Turkish tables for centuries.

## Ingredients You Need for Mercimek Corbasi

Creating an authentic bowl of Mercimek Corbasi requires a few key ingredients, most of which are pantry staples. The beauty lies in their quality and the way they come together.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show! Ensure they are split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily for that signature creamy texture. About 1 cup is usually sufficient.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. One medium onion and 2-3 cloves of garlic, finely chopped, will build a robust flavor base.
*   **Tomato Paste:** Adds depth of flavor and a lovely reddish hue. A tablespoon or two is generally enough.
*   **Flour (optional but recommended):** A tablespoon of all-purpose flour can be used to create a roux with the aromatics, helping to thicken the soup and give it a smoother consistency.
*   **Butter or Olive Oil:** For sautéing the aromatics and for the final flavor-packed topping. Turkish cuisine often favors butter for richness.
*   **Water or Vegetable/Chicken Broth:** Approximately 6-7 cups. Broth will add more flavor, but water works perfectly fine.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** Essential for the classic Turkish flavor. Used both in the soup and especially in the butter topping.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras/Urfa Pepper):** Adds a mild warmth and a beautiful visual appeal to the topping. Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** Crucial for serving, providing a bright, tangy counterpoint that elevates the entire dish.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Mercimek Corbasi

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl every time:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse 1 cup of red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any impurities and excess starch. Drain well and set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter (or olive oil) over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Build the Base:** Stir in 1-2 tablespoons of tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. If using flour, sprinkle 1 tablespoon of all-purpose flour over the onion mixture and cook for another minute, stirring to create a light roux. This will help thicken your Mercimek Corbasi.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in 6-7 cups of water or broth. Season with 1 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper.
5.  **Simmer and Cook:** Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very soft and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend to Smoothness:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.
7.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt and pepper if needed. Stir in 1 teaspoon of dried mint.
8.  **Prepare the Topping (Nane Yağı):** In a small saucepan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in 1-2 teaspoons of dried mint and 1-2 teaspoons of red pepper flakes (pul biber). The residual heat will infuse the butter without burning the spices.
9.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the aromatic butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi Results

While the recipe is simple, a few expert tips can elevate your Mercimek Corbasi from good to absolutely unforgettable.

*   **Rinse Those Lentils!** Don't skip rinsing. It removes starch, which can make the soup cloudy, and any dust or debris.
*   **Sautéing is Key:** Take your time with the onions and garlic. Properly caramelizing them builds a deep flavor base that will shine through in the final soup. Cook the tomato paste for a minute too; this removes its raw taste and enhances its sweetness.
*   **Don't Overlook the Flour (if using):** The small amount of flour, when cooked briefly with the aromatics, creates a slight roux that contributes significantly to the soup's velvety texture without making it heavy.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** The signature of a great Mercimek Corbasi is its smooth, almost pureed consistency. Blend thoroughly until there are no visible lentil pieces left.
*   **The Power of the Topping:** The *nane yağı* (mint and pepper infused butter) is non-negotiable. It adds an incredible aroma, a beautiful color, and a burst of flavor that truly distinguishes this soup. Don't cook the mint and pepper flakes in the butter for too long, as they can burn quickly.
*   **Fresh Lemon is a Must:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating cuts through the richness, brightens the flavors, and adds an essential tanginess that balances the soup beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Turkish Lentil Soup

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Traditionally, it's served as a starter, but it's hearty enough to be a light meal on its own.

*   **Lemon Wedges:** This is non-negotiable. Always serve with fresh lemon wedges, allowing each diner to add as much zest as they desire.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A slice of warm, crusty bread (like Turkish pide or a good sourdough) is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the delicious soup.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or dill can add a touch of freshness and color.
*   **Yogurt (Optional):** Some people enjoy a small dollop of plain yogurt swirled into their soup for an added creamy tang, though this is less traditional for Mercimek Corbasi compared to other Turkish soups.
*   **Pickles:** A side of Turkish pickled vegetables (turşu) offers a sharp, briny contrast that pairs wonderfully with the soup's richness.
*   **As a Starter:** Serve small bowls of this warming Turkish lentil soup before a main course of grilled meats, rice pilaf, or vegetable dishes.

## Variations and Substitutions for Mercimek Corbasi

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is perfect as is, there are a few ways you can adapt it to suit your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Make it Vegan:** Simply use olive oil instead of butter for sautéing and for the topping. Ensure your broth is vegetable-based.
*   **Gluten-Free:** If you're avoiding gluten, you can omit the flour from the recipe. The lentils will still naturally thicken the soup, though it might be slightly thinner. Alternatively, use a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend.
*   **Add Vegetables:** While not traditional, some variations include finely diced carrots or potatoes added with the lentils to simmer, for extra nutrients and texture.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the topping to your preference. For more heat, you can also add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the soup itself.
*   **Broth Boost:** While water works fine, using vegetable or chicken broth instead of water will imbue the soup with a deeper, more complex flavor.
*   **Herb Alternatives:** While dried mint is iconic for Mercimek Corbasi, you could experiment with a tiny pinch of dried oregano or thyme if you're looking for a different aromatic profile, though mint remains the most authentic choice.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a red lentil soup; it's an experience of Turkish comfort and culinary heritage. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor that is truly captivating. Whether you're making it for a family meal, a cozy evening in, or to impress guests, this nourishing and delicious soup is sure to become a beloved addition to your recipe repertoire. Give it a try, and let the warmth of Turkey fill your kitchen and your soul.
